caption:
Why watch women sports? 
Being a female athlete, you hear this said a lot. It may be when you’re informing people you have an upcoming race, or if the sport is on tv, but it means the male sport channel would have to be switched, or even by family and friends. Watching women athletics may not seem like a lot, but it’s our world.

I have never worked continuously so hard for something in my life. Giving up holidays, vacations, funerals, having a “normal” college experience. Gaining a life long injury and fighting to not medically retire. Questioning if I could make it through the day, let alone the rest of the season. After 8 years, I would do it all over again. I would “give up” the same things if it meant I could row.

This sport has led me to have the experience of a life time. The experience of teamwork, friendship, pain, dedication, growth, triumph, and failure. God has blessed me, and all of us female athletes, with an amazing once in a life time opportunity. That is the college experience. The lessons we learn in our sport is what life is all about. It’s the reward of persevering through all of life’s obstacles. It’s looking for the small wins when all seems lost. It’s getting up and putting your nose to the grindstone for months just for one goal.

Why watch women’s sports? 
Because we do the same thing as men. We may not have the fastest times known to mankind, but we set records. We win the same, we race the same, we train the same, we want it the same.

To all the female athletes out there, you are worth watching. You are worth changing the channel for and to be applauded for your hard work. Don’t let people who are unwilling to open their minds to the fact that you matter. Don’t let people who don’t have a clue about the blood, sweat, and tears you put in make you feel any less of an athlete. Those who don’t get what it’s like to live day by day for your sport. I am so beyond proud of every one of you I have met and I pray you have an abundance of support and blessings!
#ngwsd

caption:
to all my fellow female-athletes, current, former, and future…

what a gift it is to be able to embody both beauty and strength, grace and passion, love and courage. what a gift it is to be able to celebrate each other, not for what we’ve accomplished, but for who we are. what a gift it is to take fire meant to burn us down and use it to forge ourselves into gold. 

today we come together not only as women, not only as athletes, but as people whose hearts are on fire for a sport we fight hard for. i know some of you have broken dreams. i know some of you have been forced to walk away too soon. i know some of you have scars you’ll never show from something that was supposed to be “fun.” each of us have stories we could share and burdens we could bear with one another, and though there’s a lot of hard that binds them together, there’s a whole lot of good too. 

being a female-athlete isn’t just about being female, and it isn’t just about being an athlete either. it’s about being who God created you to be, made in His image, made for this moment. our bodies can do amazing things. but our hearts? our souls? the stuff on the inside you can’t see? that’s what really counts. 

our sports break us. mentally, physically, emotionally… there’s so much hard that isn’t talked about, so many challenges most people will never see. but not our Maker. no, He will take that hurt, He will take those wounds, and He will heal and He will use it for something bigger and better. our Author isn’t just writing our stories… He’s walking it with us. 

so, to all my fellow female-athletes.. hold your heads high. you’re a daughter of the King my dear.

you’re royalty. 
you’re chosen. 
you’re cherished. 
you’re held. 
you’re seen. 
you’re known. 
you’re loved.

athlete.name: Faith Osamuyi
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a fierce determination, this sprinter effortlessly blends speed and agility. Hailing from a vibrant athletic background, her infectious enthusiasm inspires teammates while chasing lightning-fast dreams on the track.

caption:
We see you Faith 🇳🇬

With college bests of 7.48s in the 60m and 8.28s in the 60m hurdles, Faith Osamuyi 🇳🇬 has wasted no time announcing herself on the collegiate stage.

In her freshman year at @alabamatrack, Faith has been moving differently, showing composure, range, and consistency across both the sprints and hurdles during the 2026 indoor season. At the Indiana Invitational, she impressed by finishing 2nd in the 60m prelims before placing 5th in the finals, and then delivered a commanding performance in the hurdles winning the 60mH final in 8.41s after qualifying 3rd.

She carried that form into the Orange & Purple Invite, where she continued to sharpen her edge. Faith clocked 7.48s in the 60m to set a college best and followed it up with a standout 8.28s in the 60m hurdles, also a college best, while contesting multiple rounds against strong competition.

Before moving to the United States, Faith was based in Benin, Nigeria, where she laid her foundation under the guidance of Coach Anthony Bamidele Moses before relocating to pursue her academic studies and track career. That grounding is evident in her poise and execution as she transitions seamlessly into collegiate competition.

With her freshman year still unfolding, Faith is just getting started and there’s much more to come as she continues to raise the bar indoors and beyond. 🇳🇬🔥

caption:
Thank You Jesus Christ, for Football,

It is with a deeply heavy, yet peaceful and content heart that, after two back-to-back ACL reconstructive surgeries and a recent ACL & Meniscus repair surgery earlier in the season, I will be medically retiring from football.

✝️ Most importantly, I would love to thank my Lord and Savior, Jesus Christ, for saving me and setting me on this journey to be as Christ-like as possible through the sport of football, and for the incredible family He has blessed me with through football and through the University of Alabama.
🧑‍🧑‍🧒‍🧒 Secondly, none of this would be possible without the unconditional love, support, and seen and unseen sacrifices of my Mom, Dad, and Little Sister. I cannot thank you three, embodiments-of-love, enough for raising me, teaching me countless lessons, and always being present with me no matter what.
🐘 I would love to thank Coach Saban and his staff for blessing me with the opportunity to be a part of this program. I would also love to thank Coach DeBoer and his staff. Every individual who made up each of these two unique staffs have helped me strive to be the best possible version of myself and overcome adversity.
🤝 I’d like to thank my teammates for the blessed bonds of brotherhood we’ve formed over the years that will last a lifetime.
🏴‍☠️ I would love to thank Coach Nichols and Coach Kervin and their staff for developing me for the next level and for helping me enjoy the thrill of high school ball and all it had to offer.
⚜️ I would love to thank Coach Reed, Coach French, and the Saints & BT family for teaching me discipline, commitment, and loving one another through thick and thin while growing up with football.
🍢 I would love to thank Coach Ellington, Coach Lickovitch, and the Seminole family for welcoming me to my very first football team and introducing me to brotherhood and the heart-thumping, exciting, and fun game that is football.

It is time for a redirection and the continuation of God’s plan in my life. This is not the end. This is only the beginning.

Thank Each and Every One of You. God Bless You. 🙏🏈 #rolltide #bpsiphi

athlete.bio: Josh Cuevas combines agility and tenacity as a tight end for Alabama. Hailing from a small town, his work ethic and relentless drive mirror his passion for the game and community.

caption:
Words can’t begin to describe the deep sense of gratitude I feel as my college football career comes to an end…As some may know, my journey to get to Alabama wasn’t straight by any means but that ultimately shaped me as both a player and a person. Cal Poly, Washington, and Alabama all played a vital role in my development. I’m extremely thankful for every person that I crossed paths with, whether it be coaches, teammates, nutritionists, academic staff, or medical personnel. At one point they all believed in me, challenged me, and prepared me enough for the next level, on and off the field. The lessons learned through adversity, leadership, and perseverance will stay with me far beyond the game I play. Lastly, to my family and friends: thank you for your unwavering support, sacrifices, and belief in me through every high and low. Your presence and love carried me through this journey, and I have never taken it for granted for a single second.

As I take this next step and declare for the 2026 NFL Draft, I do so with humility, focus, and purpose. I’m grateful for everything that brought me here and every road I went down for it motivates me to conquer what lies ahead. Let it be known that the tide always rises…What an honor it is to have ever worn that crimson and white.

Roll Tide,
Josh Cuevas 🤟🏼

caption:
The Patriot All-America. What an absolute honor to be a part of such an incredible event for a second year. From a golf standpoint, it was not the week I was hoping for, however I am forever grateful to be a part of a tournament that is so meaningful. 

At the beginning of the Patriot each player is given a bag with the name of a fallen veteran that the player will carry throughout the week. This year I received the bag representing Police Officer Chris Yung. Officer Yung was just 18 years old when he served for the US Marine Corps in Iraq. After returning home, Officer Yung joined the Prince William County Police Department in the Traffic Unit. After seven years of service in the department, Officer Yung was tragically killed in a motorcycle accident on December 31, 2012.

I think many times in our busy lives we tend to take for granted all we have and all we are able to do. It is because of these brave men and women who sacrifice everything for our freedoms that we are able to live the lives we choose. I am honored to be able to participate in an event such as the Patriot that gives back to our veterans and brings attention to all they have done for us. Thank you to our soldiers, our police officers, our firefighters, and all of their families for the sacrifices they have made for us.

caption:
“gratitude”

i had no idea how much this word would grow when God put it on my heart in november of 2024. i had no idea how much of an anthem it would become, not only for me, but also for so many others. i had no idea it would be the backbone for some of the most challenging moments athletically and personally, or how much goodness and beauty would flow from it. 

i had no idea, but God knew all along. 

there really isn’t any other word i’d rather use to sum up the year than this one. gratitude for the dark days because they prepare you for the good ones, and gratitude for the wonderful times that far outweigh any nasty moment. 

many of my friends and i are about to step into a season with a whole lot of lasts… the end of athletic careers, completing degrees, and parting ways with so many wonderful people. but we’re also stepping into a season with a whole lot of new… so much opportunity awaits… a whole lot of life to live. 

through all of this, it’s the little moments. it’s the memories you make when you don’t even realize you’re making them. it’s the sunrise over the river, the laughing until you can’t breathe, and the showing up when you need someone there. life will keep going, but there’s always time for gratitude. sure, it’s a new year, but some things are worth holding onto, worth keeping, worth growing, worth fighting for. 

Jesus came so that we may have eternal life, but he also came so we can live life here to the fullest. as one year closes and another one begins, let us continue to press into His faithful
embrace, loving big and living well. 

gratitude… for it all 🤍

“then Christ will make his home in your hearts as you trust in him. your roots will grow down into God’s love and keep you strong. and may you have the power to understand, as all God’s people should, how wide, how long, how high, and how deep his love is. may you experience the love of Christ, though it is too great to understand fully. then you will be made complete with all the fullness of life and power that comes from God.” ephesians‬ ‭3‬:‭17‬-‭19‬

The Charlotte, NC native is averaging (15.5) points, (4.4) rebounds, and (3.0) assists per game, while shooting an efficient 47.4% from the field, 44.4% from three, and 83.3% from the free-throw line. A poised 5’8” guard who can score at all three levels, Timmons combines shot-making with smart decision-making and steady leadership in the Crimson Tide backcourt.

She plays with purpose spacing the floor, knocking down timely shots, and creating opportunities for others while staying efficient and composed.

A veteran scorer with polish, toughness, and trust in big moments Jessica Timmons is setting the tone early for Alabama. ✨🏀

athlete.name: Olaus Alinen
athlete.bio: Olaus Alinen, a Finnish powerhouse, combines grit with finesse on the offensive line. Known for his relentless work ethic and tactical prowess, he embodies resilience and camaraderie, forging paths for teammates.

caption: What a meaningful day. I’m thankful to God and super blessed to have my family with me to celebrate this moment. I’ve missed so many meaningful milestones prioritizing my career over the years. I left my high school in Finland after my freshman year, foregoing graduating and building lifelong memories with my best friends. In Connecticut, I was blessed to be part of an amazing, tight knit, community at The Loomis Chaffee School. However, to early enroll in college and get a jump start on my athletic career here at Alabama, I was forced to drop out and get my GED after my senior football season. Unfortunately they never budged on giving me my degree early, so this is the first graduation I’ve ever truly been a part of. These past 3 years have been some of the best, but also most challenging years of my life. I’m grateful to have the opportunity to play at this great university, create memories for a lifetime with my brothers, and complete my degree. Finishing my undergrad in finance & economics in 3 years with a 4.0 GPA was not only a goal to me, but it was something personal. I wanted to have something that nobody can ever take away from me. I am incredibly proud and grateful to say that I am a graduate of The University of Alabama, for life. #rolltide

athlete.name: Corinne Bunagan
athlete.bio: A tenacious competitor with a flair for artistry, this All-Around powerhouse blends agility and precision. Known for her infectious enthusiasm, she inspires teammates while captivating crowds with every breathtaking routine.

caption:
Amor Fati- in love with fate
I recently got this phrase tattooed as a reminder to myself to show gratitude for every part of my journey, the highs and the lows. Every challenge I’ve been through has made me the person I am today and I love doing life with her.
I recently tore my ACL in practice, ending my gymnastics career. I love this sport with all my heart and my time at Alabama has changed me forever. While I want nothing more than to compete in Coleman one last time, I look back on my career with no regrets. If I could talk to the girl who started this journey two decades ago, she would be so proud of how far we’ve come. Gymnastics, you will forever be my first love. I don’t know who I’d be without this sport to shape me. The game changes but the skills remain, I will take what I’ve learned into every aspect of my life. I finish this chapter with such overwhelming gratitude. To experience something as special as gymnastics and to finish it at the university of my dreams is more than I could’ve ever asked for. 

Thank you to my coaches, friends, and family who made this possible. The journey wouldn’t have happened without you and I’m forever grateful for the part everyone took in it.

Although I won’t be on the floor flipping, I’ll still be with Team 52 the rest of the year. This group of girls has something special and I can’t wait for them to show the world. As always, roll tide♥️

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor from a small town, this outside hitter fuses strategic finesse with raw power, embodying resilience and charisma. Off the court, she inspires teammates with her infectious enthusiasm.

caption:
Twelve years of volleyball. More than half of my life. This sport has been a part of me for so long that it still does not feel real that it is actually over. These past four years have brought some of the best and hardest moments of my life. My journey was never easy, but I would not change a single thing. Volleyball gave me so much more than wins and losses. It gave me my people. The girls I laughed with every day, who saw me at my best and my absolute worst, and who became my best friends. That is the part I will miss the most.

To my teammates and best friends, thank you for every memory, every laugh, every bus ride, and every coffee trip. You all made this experience what it was. You became my family and my constants. I truly mean it when I say I would not have made it through these years without you. Leaving volleyball is so hard because I do not get to show up next to you every day and compete. I love you all more than you will ever know, and I am so grateful that this sport brought me each of you.

And to everyone who supported me, thank you. To my family, my coaches, my friends, and anyone who ever showed up for me in the biggest or smallest ways, thank you from the bottom of my heart. Every message, every hug, every word of encouragement, every person who believed in me when I was tired, frustrated, or doubting myself, it all meant more than you know. Your support carried me through the hardest days and made the best moments even sweeter. I hope you all know how much that meant to me.

Walking away is hard, but I am leaving with a full heart. I got to live out my childhood dream for four amazing years, and not many people get to say that. Volleyball gave me friendships and memories that I will cherish forever, and I am so grateful for every second of these past twelve years. I am closing this this chapter of my life and excited to see what is next.🤍🤍
RTR forever and #16 out✌🏼✌🏼✌🏼

caption:
This month we celebrate my Paps, Happy belated birthday, Dad. I hope you know how deeply you are admired, not just for how hard you work or how much you sacrifice, but for the love you give so freely to your family. You are the most dedicated father I know, steady in your strength and always leading with both humor and heart. You protect, you provide, and you lift us up even on the days we don’t say thank you loud enough. Your presence fills a room, your laughter brings us together, and the love you have shown me has shaped my entire life in ways I will never forget. I am who I am because of you, because you taught me what love, resilience, and devotion look like. Thank you for everything this month we celebrate you. 

Because of you, we grew up knowing what love, strength, and family truly mean. You raised us to be thoughtful, selfless, and resilient, to care for each other the way you have always cared for us. The values you taught us, the warmth you carried, the love you showed even when life wasn’t easy, all of it shaped us into the people we are today. We are a reflection of your heart, your dedication, and the way you love without hesitation. You didn’t just raise children, you raised a family built on loyalty, respect, and unbreakable bonds, and that is one of the greatest gifts you could have ever given us.
Happy Birthday, Dad. ❤️

caption:
hello everyone! With the conclusion of campaigning coming up, along with being two days out from voting, I wanted to share my “why” and the inspiration behind my efforts during this homecoming season.

as some of you may know, I am a student-athlete on the track and cross-country team and although it has brought me two sec XC team titles, the most amazing people, and experiences, it has also brought a lot of injuries and health issues that have made it extremely difficult to run and reach my athletic goals. 

I haven’t had a roommate since my freshman year of college, so sometimes coming home after a long day of practice and school, especially through injury, was hard not having someone there to express all that was going through my mind.

over fall break my junior year, my team was traveling to a race which I was unable to attend due to injury. my sadness of not being able to attend pushed me to participate in a program I had heard about called “Happy Hour,” which is hosted by Tuscaloosa Metro Animal Shelter.

The moment I took Princess out for the day, I knew I had to adopt her. I felt like her presence was what I had been missing. It was nice to have someone there who was always smiling and I felt like everything would be ok when she was around. I had always told myself that my worth was found in my sport, but Princess helped me realize that your worth is found in how you treat those around you.

After a few weeks, I was able to officially adopt Princess, and this month, it has officially been one year since she joined our family. Princess has only strengthened my passion to help all shelter animals find their forever home. Not only has Princess helped me find my joy, but I would like to think I’ve done the same for her. Whether it was giving her a new, fluffy bed, taking her on a boat for the first time, or spoiling her with maybe one too many pup cups, I know that I am filling her cup, just as she has mine. 

It is never too late to foster or adopt any of these deserving animals. I know that I was able to save her, but I think she saved me too💗💗💗

Yesterday, Mattie and I were able to visit Tuscaloosa Metro Animal Shelter! Not only were we able to drop off over ONE HUNDRED donations for animals in need, we were also fortunate enough to take a few adoptable dogs out for some exercise! Here is some info about them!

Mio is a two year old pitbull mix who is so sweet and energetic, but can also be the best snuggle buddy. She is perfect for anyone who is active or someone who enjoys a good movie night as well.

Officer is a one year old pitbull/lab who would be perfect for someone who lives an active lifestyle. He is the longest resident at Metro and has his adoption fee waived. He is seriously the sweetest boy!

With the holiday season coming up, it’s so important to give these animals a place to go. Every single one of them deserves a warm and welcoming place. Mio and Officer are two of the many animals who are all waiting for their forever home. Please consider fostering or adopting one of these cuties for the holiday season!

caption:
Ending this chapter in my life with a grateful heart. For the past 15 years gymnastics has been my whole world. It has given me a purpose and opened so many endless opportunities. This isn’t an easy decision but I’ve decided that it’s in my best interest mentally and physically to take a step away from the sport. I’m forever grateful to represent the Script A and BAMA will always hold a special place in my heart. I’m excited for the next chapter in my life. Gods plan always.

Thank you to my coaches throughout my life that have helped me get to where i am today. It’s truly been an honor to learn and grow from all of you and I couldn’t thank you guys enough.

To my teammates, you guys are what keeps me going. My rocks. My heart. I’m grateful for the memories that we have together. You all have stuck by my side day 
in and day out and I couldn’t show my appreciation towards all of you enough. You guys don’t know how much y’all mean to me. It’s US FOREVER. I love you guys. 

To my family, thank you for being my foundation. You all have truly never given up on me and my dreams and I wouldn’t be here without your love and support. You’ve helped me accomplish a dream of mine and I’ve never wished for anything more. 

To the little girl with big dreams, I’m so proud of you.

caption:
Hi Y’all! I’m Sydney Blackhurst, a junior from Gilbert, Arizona, majoring in Accounting. I’m so excited and grateful to announce my candidacy and campaign for Homecoming Queen 2025!

My campaign, “Believed In,” comes from my own story. After facing chronic illness, I learned how powerful it is to have people believe in you- especially when it feels hard to believe in yourself.

That lesson led me to found Beyond Barriers Swim Foundation, a nonprofit that provides adaptive swim lessons for children with disabilities and chronic conditions. Our goal is simple: to give every child an extra person to believe in them- in and out of the water.

If given this opportunity, I’ll continue that mission by supporting the UA Rise Center, helping children grow, feel capable, and know they’re believed in.
Thank you, UA, for giving me a place where belief turns into purpose!
 #BelievedIn #Homecoming2025

caption:
Good afternoon, UA! My name is Crawford West and I’m a senior from Birmingham, Alabama studying public health and sales.

I am honored to have been selected for this year’s homecoming court, which puts me in the running for Homecoming Queen!

I have had the incredible honor of representing our university as a student-athlete on the cross-country and track team for the past 3.5 years. Being able to represent my incredible team on homecoming court has already been such a blessing. I wouldn’t be half the person I am today without them.

Tuscaloosa has not only given me the most amazing school, opportunities, and friends, but it’s also given me my best friend Princess. I adopted Princess a year ago, and it was easily the best decision. Her resilience to keep smiling despite her challenges inspires me to live my life the same way.

I will be advocating for the Paws of UA, an on campus club that directly benefits the Tuscaloosa Metro Animal Shelter (where I adopted Princess from). I am honored to have this platform to share a cause and place that I’m so passionate about during a week that is so meaningful to our school.

caption:
Hi everyone! My name is Rachel Rybicki, I am a senior pursuing a degree with a double major in Finance and Economics, and a minor in Spanish.  I am so honored and excited to announce my candidacy and campaign for Homecoming Queen. 

Service has shaped who I am as an individual. Connecting with others, serving them, and learning about their stories is something that I am very passionate about. My past 3 years in Tuscaloosa have been shaped by the time I have spent investing in the education of the students at Flatwoods Elementary. Education can provide so many opportunities, and my goal is to support children as they gain a foundational education to set them up for their futures. 

I am running for Homecoming Queen to be able to share my story with the hopes of inspiring others to find their purpose or passion. I hope to bring a spotlight to childhood education and service. I have experienced and embraced the culture and community that we have here at The University of Alabama, and having the opportunity to run for Homecoming Queen and represent our Script A is an honor!
#RisewithRachel #UniversityofAlabama #EmpowerThroughEducation

caption:
Introducing Varsity Athlete Cole Adams and the VW-03.

Sales of this model directly support Cole a football player at the University of Alabama. For each piece sold of this model, Cole will receive $50 from Varsity Watch. 

Cole Adams embodies the world-class speed, competitive excellence, and remarkable resilience that defines Alabama Crimson Tide football. 

As a redshirt freshman wide receiver, Adams represents the Crimson Tide after an exceptional high school career at Owasso High School in Oklahoma, where he demonstrated elite athleticism both on the football field and track. His junior season showcased his explosive potential with 55 receptions for 913 yards and eight touchdowns, while also returning three kickoffs and two punts for touchdowns. 

Adams possesses legitimate world-class speed, posting remarkable times of 6.98 seconds in the indoor 60 meters, 10.65 seconds in the 100 meters, and 22.27 seconds in the 200 meters, making him one of the fastest players in college football. His 2024 season demonstrated both his emerging talent and incredible grit, as he earned his first career start at wide receiver against South Carolina despite playing through multiple injuries, contributing 6 catches for 94 yards while serving as Alabama’s primary punt returner. 

Adams exemplified true toughness by continuing to compete at the highest level even while battling through arm and leg injuries that ultimately ended his season, with coach Kalen DeBoer praising “the effort he put into that first injury” and noting “the toughness he has” as defining characteristics. 

Beyond his athletic achievements, Adams demonstrated exceptional character and leadership at Owasso, spending much of his time mentoring special needs students and serving as a positive influence in his community. As a proud ambassador for Varsity Watch, Adams represents the values of speed, character, resilience, and competitive excellence that make him a valuable asset both on the field and in promoting the brand’s commitment to supporting student-athletes who combine elite performance with genuine leadership and the grit to overcome adversity.

caption:
if you know me, you’re probably aware that writing is a huge piece of my life. for years, my journal has been a private place to pour out my thoughts, prayers, worries, joys, fears, dreams, and gratitudes. my words have been a safe spot for the cries of my heart to land, a window into the reality of who Jesus Christ is. 

but here’s the thing. 

those journals? there are pieces inside meant to be shared. 
those words? not my own… never were to begin with. 

for years i’ve been encouraged to make my private writings public. my response has always been the same: “one day.” and here we are… “one day” is now today. 

there isn’t a flow or rhythm to this account other than words that reflect the breathings of my heart. habakkuk was told by God to simply record, and that is what i am here to do as well. i hope these words can be a window for you as they have been for me, to grasp even a slightly clearer picture of the beautiful Truth of who and whose you are. as sweet Jesus speaks to me through pen and paper, i pray you hear His whisper and feel His nudge. as you see glimpses of my own heart, i hope you feel less alone and a whole lot more seen… because friend, you are more than seen. you are known, and you are loved. 

so here we are, taking a small step. 

welcome to “words and a window.” 

“then the LORD replied: ‘write down the revelation and make it plain on tablets so that a herald may run with it...’.” habakkuk 2:2 

<3 hal

athlete.bio: A tenacious forward hailing from the heart of Alabama, this player's relentless drive and tactical acumen redefine the game. Known for creativity on the field and an infectious passion off it.

caption:
Trusting God through breaking my foot was one of the hardest things i’ve ever done.It first started in december when I broke it, and apparently it never healed and I played on it for three months broken. just about 2 weeks before my club team went to nationals. I broke it again at practice. Learning that my foot was never actually healed and I had to get surgery. I have never had surgery before.The hard part is missing out on my last time ever playing with the girls and coach i grew up with. but the HARDEST part is coming into my freshman year with a broken foot.... i leave for college in 4 days. this wasn’t how i expected to go in to college. But above all this chaos Gods word and plan is above mine and what i wanted. and i just know that God works in mysterious ways. and i will come back even stronger and better than i was before. Bet ready SEC!
God IS good and i KNOW he’s not done with me yet:)

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with an unyielding spirit, this distance runner thrives on the thrill of the chase, blending grit and grace. Passionate about pushing limits, they inspire teammates with unwavering determination.

caption: Freshman year has been such a huge learning experience for me. It has taught me so much both on and off the track, but most importantly I learned that you never truly know what a person is going through. Soon after losing my childhood coach, on November 19, 2024, I got into an accident. This was a huge turning point, and it made me question everything. It left me uncertain about my future. I wasn't able to attend any of my classes and I didn't know the next time I'd be able to compete, but something told me this was just a setback and not the end. Every step forward, no matter how small it was, I considered a win. I'd come too far to give up. Although track is a huge part of my life, I witnessed firsthand how quickly it could be taken away. With that being said, I took everything I went through freshman year as a lesson and a reason to keep pushing forward to do what I love most because the things you take for granted, someone else is praying for. Life itself is a gift... be grateful always❤️

caption:
Tomorrow, I will make history. As a first-generation college student, I’ll be walking across the stage—not to receive my first degree, but my second. God, I thank You.
My name, Miracle, truly defines my journey. Academics haven’t always come easy. I was diagnosed with ADHD in kindergarten, and the road has never been straight. There were times I didn’t think I’d make it. But here I am—about to graduate with my bachelor’s degree in Human Environmental Science!
By God’s grace, and through the blessing of competing as a student-athlete, I’ve been able to finish school debt-free. That’s a gift I don’t take for granted.
To my momma—thank you. You taught me how to advocate for myself and find the resources I needed. Your strength helped me find my own. This degree isn’t just for me—it’s for you.

athlete.name: Steijn Louter
athlete.bio: Hailing from a rich swimming tradition, this breaststroker blends power and finesse in every stroke. Known for an infectious enthusiasm and relentless work ethic, he embodies the spirit of competition.

caption:
One week before the only qualification (for European under 23 championship) race that truly mattered, one wrong move, a sharp twist in my hip changed the situation. My groin didn’t tear, but it held me back just enough to remind me how fragile momentum can be. How quickly plans can shift.

I could’ve chosen to race. Push through the discomfort. Show up simply because I could. But that’s not why I train. I don’t dedicate hours, energy, and focus just to show up half-ready. I aim to be fully present in body and in mind.

Sometimes strength means standing still. Listening. Choosing patience over pride. It’s recognizing that progress isn’t always loud. That sometimes, the most powerful move is the one you don’t make. It’s not about giving up; it’s about protecting the bigger picture. Trusting the process. Strategy over impulse. Wisdom over ego. Long-term over short-term.

Stepping back isn’t weakness. It’s preparation. Each quiet day is an opportunity, to recover, to reflect, to refine. And when I return, it won’t be rushed. It’ll be with clarity, intention, and nothing wasted.

Because I’m not chasing moments.
I’m building something that lasts. Peace out! 👊🏼❤️

caption:
2025 indoor season

I got my first collegiate win in the first ever heptathlon I competed in, finally got a pole vault personal best after 3 years, and I came 4th at SEC’s. These are just a few of the highlights from my indoor season. The best moment being my coach telling me right before my 1k race at SEC’s, “you’re going to love the 1k”, which has been a joke all season. I ended up running a 2:31 to move up from 8th to 4th in the final event of the hep. Coach gave me a quote before the meet and I don’t think it could have been more fitting.

“I shall either find a way or make one”

All glory to God

caption:
“As student-athletes at the University of Alabama, we are proud to support the fight against suicide. Mental health is a critical issue worldwide, and it’s important to address it. The pressure to succeed—both as athletes and students—can take a toll on our well-being. That’s why it’s essential to check in on friends and loved ones, offering support even when struggles aren’t visible. Together, we can help break the stigma and create a culture of awareness and compassion.”

It is a privilege to have Graham Roten, Germie Bernard, Kaydn Proctor, Ty Simpson, Wilkin Formby, LT Overton, Michael Lorino, and the rest of the Alabama football team as ambassadors for The Fight Against Suicide.

Join us in supporting The Fight Against Suicide by donating or simply sharing this message.

caption: Thank you Lord! I’ve been a lot of places, I’ve played against some of the best players in the country and I’ve played some schools with shooting houses beside the stadium I’ve played in college stadiums for State Titles and I’ve played on fields with only one goal post. There’s been mountains and Lord knows there has been valleys. I have been so extremely blessed to have met some awesome people every step of the way and had some great men lead me. I’ve learned so much about life and who I am and about people. I’ve seen good and I have seen bad. This game and the people connected to it, can impact a man at a pivotal time in his life and I’m blessed to be apart of it. To Moody I am thankful for men I can call family for taking a kid in from a school that was a rival and treating as one of their own. I wanna thank Coach Ganus and Coach Biles Coach BC everyone in the community and staff for the greatest 9months I could have asked for. It felt like years we came so close and accomplished so much I am eternally grateful for everyone there. I was blessed to play two season for the town I was born to at Southside Coach Holcomb impacted my life tremendously and I will always be thankful for that and the relationship I made there and memories. I am grateful to everyone who has continued to support me. I wanna thank Westbrook for giving me some lifelong friends that would come watch me in freezing temperatures play for a school none of them knew existed just 3 years ago. I am so thankful for everyone that has been with me every step of this journey whether you prayed on my downfall or you prayed on my success you were needed in this journey. God has shown me so much favor in my career and I’ve been so blessed. I wanna thank everyone who came to seem me play I have the greatest family and friends no matter where I was playing or the weather I had people there or watching from across the country. As one chapter ends another one is begins. The chapter of my life has shaped who I am today through adversity and success joy and frustration everything you could imagine. The book is written I am simply turning the pages and trusting the Lord! College Ball 🔜 #27out for now

caption:
My collegiate athletic journey has been a testimonial to my faith. Here is my story. 

💔 Ever since I immigrated to this country and learned about college ball, all I wanted to be was an Alabama football player, so it was a blessing when I was offered a PWO out of high school. After stepping out onto the practice field with the team for the first time the summer before my freshman year, and going through summer workouts and Fall Camp, I unfortunately ended up tearing my ACL for the first time, one week before we kicked off the season against Utah State. I rehabbed through the season and made it back for winter workouts and Spring Ball, only to retear the same ACL halfway through the summer leading into my Sophomore year. I had gone through back-to-back rehabbing years. Those were some of the toughest battles, mentally and physically, I’ve faced. I was in my most depressed state and my heart shattered not being able to be out there practicing the sport I love with my brothers. Having to watch and cheer them on from the training room and through the weight room windows everyday while I rehabilitated my knee.

✝️ That was when I fixed my eyes and invested my faith on our Lord Jesus, more than I had ever before, I slowly learned to keep my chin up regardless of the circumstances and to never give up on hope. Even when I couldn’t comprehend or be at peace at why I had to undergo such injuries, all I could focus on was my next step. Putting one foot in front of the other. Literally and metaphorically. For God has the ultimate plan. And even when adversities come our way, it is all for the greater plan the Lord has set in motion for us. For He knows that you are strong willed to take on those adversities. And I am gratefully blessed to be a living testimony of overcoming these overwhelming situations and having those two years of eligibility back to continue on (redshirt + medical redshirt).

❤️ I make this post to encourage you to keep up on your faith and continue to have hope. Never give up, no matter what. Even if, you are facing and overcoming your own personal struggles, you WILL overcome them. I pray for your peace and strength, in Jesus’ glorious name, Amen🙏

caption:
As of August 5th, 2023 Ruby has passed away. 

To say I’ll miss you will be a great understatement. Coming home to you was the best part of my day even if you would whine so loudly my ears would hurt and you’d scratch up my legs. I’ll always miss our bedtime cuddles and belly rubs. l’ll miss our late night drives around town or how you’d love to chase me on my scooter down the street or constantly beg for my food while I was eating. I’ll miss playing hide and seek or chasing you around the house or watching you try to attack my hand from underneath a blanket. I’ll miss your big brown eyes that held the most emotion and the soft spot behind your ear that I’d always twirl.

I’ll always remember your favorite spot on my bed and your favorite blanket and toy and your favorite foods (hot dogs and chicken). I’ll remember how much you hated the sound of plastic water bottles and plastic eggs or when we’d pop bubbles with our gum. Or how you hated your paws being touched so you’d pull your paw away when I’d try to hold it. 

You were there for me the most when I felt no one else was. You always made hard things easier and you were always there to lick away my tears. You were my best friend and always will be. I’ll always love you dearly. Getting you was the best decision I’d ever made. Thank you for the best 10 years of my life ❤️Rest in peace my sweet baby girl. You’ll be in my heart forever. I love you so much❤️. At least you’d passed in my arms in your favorite spot and not the vet. I guess that’s what you would’ve wanted

caption: 2022, hats off to you for being pretty fun. This year I had began rowing for the first time, followed by quitting 3 other sports to pursue it year round. I went to Disney for the first time accompanied by a variety of music friends, promptly followed by winter formal. I competed at Youth Nationals with my 5 other team mates and friends, becoming closer with all of them and the sport itself. A month later, I attended the Princeton Rowing camp days before flying to Europe. We visited France, Switzerland and Germany with a pit stop in Lichtenstein, and I am ecstatic to be going again next year :) Fall came around and so did fall rowing, more races and practices lead to Head of the Charles and competing for weeks in our women’s 2X, barely making time for homecoming. Once rowing had wrapped itself up for the year, my time was pretty much spent prepping for Science Olympiad and messing around with my favorite nerds. The gratitude I have for everybody I have met and have gotten to know will surely bleed into 2023. Not too shabby🎉

My love for swimming started with the Sidney-Shelby County YMCA and coaches Chad McClain and Mary Jannides. A huge thank you goes out to the Alabama swim coaches for their belief in me and vision for what we can accomplish as a team. Coach Margo, Coach White, Coach Hodgson, Coach Larson, I can’t wait to get to Tuscaloosa to work with the amazing staff and team! Finally my biggest thanks goes to my family for their unwavering support and sacrifices along my swim journey. My mom, dad, sister Addison and brothers Jaxxson, Justiss and Josseph have all helped me get to this point. And I know they’ll be cheering right along with me, Roll Tide🔴⚪️🐘!
